about: Settings VERSION 2 for FACTUAL CORRECTNESS. Same metric, judge, mode, splitting and score as version 1 (factual_correctness.json, kept unchanged with its H2 result). Version 2 changes only the REFERENCE WORDING. The H2 first-run check (2026-11-17) found the judge wrong on 3 of 5 'missing' verdicts, because our facts were written as short phrases for word-matching in retrieval recall: 'The rails are locked' reads like a statement about the machine right now, while the SOP means an instruction ('lock the rails'). Each fact below keeps its meaning and numbers; only the wording changes. LOCK RULE: never change this file after its results are seen; make a new version instead.
metric_question: Did the facts the operator needed make it into the final answer?

reference.from: the 'reference' wording in this file, one sentence per fact. Fact ids and meanings are those of retrieval_labels.json (locked 2026-11-15, still checked at run time).
wording_rules: Keep the fact's meaning and every number. Do not add a new requirement.
Take the words from the source document (FL-101 SOP / work instruction), never from any PlantMind answer.
Write an instruction as an instruction ('Lock the guide rails'), not as a state ('The rails are locked').
Add a condition only when the instruction depends on it in the source ('If the checkweigher test fails, ...').
A fact that was already clear keeps its original wording (changed: false).
reference.blind_note: Written after the v1 H2 verdicts and H2's answer were read; the faithfulness and handover reviews had already read the answers of all five cases. The wording comes from the source documents only, but no case is fully blind for v2. H1's facts were not blind in v1 either.

response_means: The final report as graded, without the REPORT CONFIDENCE and SOURCE DATA blocks, and with 'Step N:' labels removed (the actions stay). Same answer text as faithfulness v2 and factual correctness v1.

evaluator.prompts: RAGAS built-in claim-splitting and claim-checking prompts, unchanged
evaluator.steps_used: Only the reference -> answer direction, with RAGAS's own steps unchanged: split the reference into claims (ClaimDecompositionPrompt) and check each claim against the answer (NLIStatementPrompt). The score is then computed by our rule below, not by RAGAS's combined formula.
evaluator.why_not_ragas_score: Found in the RAGAS 0.4.3 source before locking v1: its 'recall' = TP / (TP + FN), where TP counts ANSWER claims backed by the reference and FN counts REFERENCE claims missing from the answer. It mixes two directions. Our rule counts reference claims only.

rules.split: RAGAS splits the reference into claims (atomicity high, coverage high)
rules.verdict: For each reference claim, the judge decides whether the answer supports it (1) or not (0)
rules.score: reference claims supported by the answer / all reference claims

first_run_check.about: Run H2 first and compare with the v1 H2 human check (judge errors on #3 star wheel, #4 rails locked, #7 restart at 60 bpm; #11 check the changeover record truly missing; #2 usual cause borderline). v2 passes if the three judge errors are gone, the truly missing fact is still missing, and the split is still sensible. A person confirms. If it fails, stop: do not tune and re-run silently.

also_report.per_fact: Map each reference claim back to its fact id (by code: the fact sharing the most words with the claim; a person confirms) so a missed fact can be compared with the grounding funnel (never found / dropped by a helper / reached the writer but left out of the answer).
also_report.wrong_value: Manual review of every MISSING fact: if the answer states the same thing with a DIFFERENT value (for example 1.4 bar where the SOP says 1.3), label it WRONG, not just missing. Quote the answer text.

manual_review_rule: A claim counts as present only with the same meaning and the same numbers; a vaguer statement does not count. Corrections are recorded as data, pointing to the review, never by editing results.

H1.reference: If the checkweigher test fails, do not start the line.
If the checkweigher test fails, call the quality lead.

H1.fact_v1: By hand it is only 5 bottles an hour
H1.reference: Weighing by hand checks only 5 bottles an hour.
In the checkweigher test, the 490 ml and 510 ml test bottles must be rejected and the 500 ml test bottle must pass.
Record the checks on the pre-start checklist.
The shift lead signs the pre-start checklist.

H2.fact_v1: 330 ml bottles need rail position B
H2.reference: For 330 ml bottles, set the guide rails to position B.

H2.fact_v1: Rails not reset after a changeover are the usual cause
H2.reference: Guide rails not reset after a bottle size changeover are the most common cause of infeed jams.

H2.fact_v1: The matching star wheel is fitted
H2.reference: Fit the star wheel that matches the bottle size.
Lock the guide rails in position.

H2.fact_v1: Stop and lock out before clearing a jam
H2.reference: Stop the machine and lock it out before clearing a jam.
When restarting, run the line at 60 bottles per minute first.
H2.source: SOP 12.2 step 6 line 293; SOP 14 step 4 line 367

H2.fact_v1: Never reach into the infeed or star wheel while running
H2.reference: Never reach into the infeed or the star wheel while the machine is running.
Wear cut-resistant gloves when removing jammed bottles.
If a changeover happened this shift, check the changeover record first.
Remove any chipped or damaged bottles from the infeed.

H2.fact_v1: The shift lead signs the changeover record
H2.reference: The shift lead signs the changeover record.

H3.fact_v1: Underfill after new seals is a reason to call the maintenance supervisor
H3.reference: Underfill that continues after the seals have been replaced is a reason to call the maintenance supervisor.

H3.fact_v1: 3 underfill alarms in one shift = a systemic fault
H3.reference: Three or more underfill alarms in one shift means a systemic fault.

H3.fact_v1: Stop production and raise a work order
H3.reference: Stop production and raise a maintenance work order.
Check whether the fill nozzle is blocked.

H3.fact_v1: Do not raise the fill time
H3.reference: Do not increase the fill time to make up for underfill.
H3.source: SOP 10 line 217; SOP 12.1 line 266; NCR section 8

H3.fact_v1: The checkweigher report shows which valves
H3.reference: The checkweigher report shows which valve numbers are underfilling.

H3.fact_v1: Supply pressure should be 1.5 to 2.0 bar
H3.reference: The product supply pressure should be 1.5 to 2.0 bar.

H3.fact_v1: A scratched valve seat stops a new seal sealing
H3.reference: A new seal will not seal on a scratched valve seat.

H3.fact_v1: NCR-2026-012 is the reason not to raise the fill time
H3.reference: NCR-2026-012 is the reason the fill time must not be raised.

H4.fact_v1: The quality lead owns QA HOLD decisions
H4.reference: The quality lead owns QA HOLD decisions.

H4.fact_v1: The quality lead signs off before restart
H4.reference: The quality lead must sign off before the line restarts.

H4.fact_v1: Clean up with the red glass kit
H4.reference: Clean up with the red glass kit.

H4.fact_v1: Use a vacuum, never compressed air
H4.reference: Use a vacuum to clean up the glass, never compressed air.

H4.fact_v1: Do not open any guard until locked out
H4.reference: Do not open any guard until the machine is locked out.

H4.fact_v1: Do not reach in until locked out
H4.reference: Do not reach into the machine until it is locked out.

H4.fact_v1: Put bottles from the last 30 minutes on QA HOLD
H4.reference: Put every bottle filled in the last 30 minutes on QA HOLD.

H4.fact_v1: Throw away open bottles within 2 metres
H4.reference: Throw away any open bottles within 2 metres of the break.

H4.fact_v1: Record it in the glass breakage log
H4.reference: Record the event in the glass breakage log.

H5.fact_v1: More than 1 in 100 over an hour: tell the shift lead
H5.reference: If the checkweigher rejects more than 1 bottle in 100 over an hour, tell the shift lead.

H5.fact_v1: A rising reject count is often the first sign of worn seals
H5.reference: A rising reject count is often the first sign of worn seals.

H5.fact_v1: Look at the fill valves for dripping
H5.reference: Look at the fill valves for dripping.

H5.fact_v1: The checkweigher report shows which valves
H5.reference: The checkweigher report shows which valve numbers are underfilling.
Weigh 5 bottles by hand to confirm.

H5.fact_v1: Do not change the fill time
H5.reference: Do not change the fill time.

H5.fact_v1: Dripping valve: maintenance replaces the seal kit
H5.reference: If a valve drips, maintenance replaces its seal kit.

H5.fact_v1: Seals every 3 months or 1,500 running hours
H5.reference: Seal kits are replaced every 3 months or every 1,500 running hours.

known_limits: An AI judge decides each verdict; a person checks the first run and every MISSING fact.
Recall does not punish made-up content; faithfulness measures that.
The reference is only the facts we listed as needed; a needed fact we forgot to list is invisible to this metric.
Rewording a fact can change how strict it is; each change is listed with its original (fact_v1) so a person can check it.
